summary: The note describes a mid-September 2023 initiative in which Havenwood High School partners with local businesses and community groups through mentorship, internships, and curriculum development. Principal Dr. Lillian Schwartz and TechForward International CEO Mr. Edgar Nielsen explain programs like 'Business Week' and the 'Junior Innovators Program', along with teacher training and service learning. The note presents the pilot as a possible nationwide template for school-community collaboration.
one_line: Havenwood High School and local businesses, led by Dr. Lillian Schwartz and Edgar Nielsen, launch partnerships offering internships, curriculum changes, and service learning.
key_facts: The note is set in mid-September 2023, the start of a new academic year, when a wave of school partnerships with local businesses and community groups is taking root.
Dr. Lillian Schwartz is the principal of Havenwood High School, a public school known for its dynamic approach to education.
Mr. Edgar Nielsen is the CEO of TechForward International, a leader in innovative technology solutions.
Havenwood High School will launch a 'Business Week' starting October 5th, 2023, in which executives and local artisans take over certain classes.
The 'Junior Innovators Program' is a joint venture between Havenwood and TechForward set to commence on November 1st, 2023.
In the Junior Innovators Program, high school juniors and seniors work alongside TechForward professionals on real projects.

Teachers are receiving specialized training from corporate trainers and community leaders to integrate practical knowledge into lessons, including collaborative lesson planning with financial analysts on the stock market and fiscal responsibility.
Social enterprises, local environmental groups, and nonprofits offer service learning opportunities that qualify for academic credit.
Jane Austen, a recent Havenwood High graduate, discovered her passion for sustainable development through an internship with GreenScape Solutions, a local environmental consultancy.
A group of tech-savvy students recently launched a start-up incubated through a school-supported program.
Success metrics include student job placements, engagement levels, and community welfare indicators.
Seasonal evaluation meetings coordinated by a joint committee keep the programs relevant.
Havenwood High School's pilot program is described as potentially a nationwide template for local education systems.
